Shri.Sunil Jacob Jose, Cgc R5 By Sr. Government Pleader Sri.Aravindakumar Babu This Writ Petition (Civil) Having Come Up For Admission On 18.01.2021, The Court On The Same Day Delivered The Following: WP(C).No.20140 Of 2012 :: 2 :: Judgment
texts.facts: Dated this the 18th day of January 2021 Petitioner in this public interest litigation is stated to be a voluntary organization registered under the Travancore-Cochin Scientific, Literary and Charitable Societies Act. Main concern raised in this public interest litigation is regarding the illegal conduct of clinical drug trials in Kerala. Hence this writ petition is filed seeking the following reliefs: "i. Issue a writ of mandamus directing the respondent Nos.2 and 3 not to permit any clinical drug trials in the State of Kerala, without the properly constituted Ethics Committees for each drug trial. ii. issue a writ of mandamus directing the respondents 2 and 3 to WP(C).No.20140 OF 2012 :: 4 :: conduct an enquiry regarding the clinical trials being conducted in the hospitals in Kerala as mentioned in Exhibit-P6 and to stop all the Clinical Drug trials which are being conducted without the properly constituted Ethics Committees and without the prior informed consent of the trial participants, in violation of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules. iii. issue a writ of mandamus directing the respondent Nos.2 and 3 to publish the details of the Ethics Committees, constituted for each Clinical Drug trial in Kerala. iv. issue a writ of mandamus directing the 3 rd respondent to take strict action to ensure that the investigator of Clinical Drug Trials should send prompt notification of all injuries or deaths, occurring during the trials 7o to respondent No. 2 and 3 and to the Institutional Ethics Committee. v. issue a writ of mandamus directing the respondent No.2 and 3 to take immediate and effective steps to ensure that the sponsors of clinical Drug trials should provide comprehensive health insurance for all trial participants to take care of all health needs or death and that the trial participants are provided immediate and long-term medical treatment and compensation for any injury or death." 6. A detailed counter affidavit has been filed on behalf of the 4 th respondent/Indian Council of Medical Research wherein, it is stated that the 4 th respondent/Indian Council of Medical Research is a body of Scientists, who do not have any regulatory powers conferred on them for the purpose of monitoring the implementation of the contents of the guidelines. It is also submitted that the 4 th respondent/Indian Council of Medical Research is only a body with technical know how and is not vested with the power of inspectors nor to monitor the implementation of the Guidelines. 7. A detailed counter affidavit has been filed on behalf of respondents 1 to 3/the Secretary, Union of India; the Drugs Controller General (India), Directorate WP(C).No.20140 OF 2012 :: 5 :: Jananeethi vs Union Of India on 18 January, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89281953/ 3
texts.arguments: 2. Adv.Daisy A.Philipose, learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner had been conducting field studies regarding the clinical drug trials in Kerala, since June 2009. During the study conducted by the petitioner, it is found that there is serious human rights violation and other harms to the participants in the clinical trials, since drug trials are being conducted without the properly constituted Ethics Committees and without the prior informed consent of the trial participants, in violation of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules. 3. It is contended by learned counsel for the petitioner that physicians receive incentives to recruit patients into trials, and do this often, without obtaining prior consent. Participants are subjected to unethical practices such as deprivation of effective medicines. Medical treatment and compensation are denied for the growing number of trial-related injuries and deaths. However, it is mandatory that all the proposals on biomedical research involving human participants should be cleared by an appropriately constituted Institutional Ethics Committee (IEC) to safeguard the welfare and the rights of the participants. According to the petitioner that it is unfortunate to note that most of the clinical WP(C).No.20140 OF 2012 :: 3 :: drug trials in Kerala is being conducted without a properly constituted Ethics Committee. 4. Another contention raised by learned counsel for the petitioner is that there are serious malpractices in the matter of obtaining the prior informed consent, from the trial participants. As per the Drugs and Cosmetic Rules and the guidelines on clinical drug trials issued by the 4 th respondent/Indian Council of Medical Research, it is mandatory that participants should be recruited for trials, only after securing their informed consent. Further, the details of drug trials, risks and possible side effects of the trials are not communicated to the participants. The patients are not given the copy of the signed informed consent form, thus depriving them of any documentary evidence to provide their participation in a given trial. According to the petitioner, this Jananeethi vs Union Of India on 18 January, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89281953/ 2 is also highly illegal and violates the fundamental right of the citizens not to be deprived of life as provided under Article 21 of the Constitution of India. 5. It is also alleged by learned counsel for the petitioner that there is no mechanisms for the State Government, for monitoring the clinical drug trials. As a result, the poor and illiterate citizens of the State of Kerala are being used as 'guinea pigs' by the drug manufacturers. It is further submitted that the Schedule Y provides that the clinical trial on a new drug shall be initiated only after permission has been granted by the licensing authority under Rule 21(b) and approval obtained from the respective Ethics Committee(s). 8. Adv.Daisy A. Philipose, learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that after the filing of the writ petition, all other reliefs sought for in the writ petition, except relief No.iii, have been Jananeethi vs Union Of India on 18 January, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89281953/ 5 addressed.
